title: Presidential Council and High State Council Members Cast Doubt on Tunis Election Deal
detail: Five days after the '4+4' committee initialled a draft election-law and elections-commission deal in Tunis, cracks opened over its legitimacy. Presidential Council head Mohamed al-Menfi warned that 'the success of any consensus is linked to the clarity of its basis, its jurisdictions, and its applicability,' criticizing the ambiguous foundation of the talks; separately, Menfi and deputy Abdullah al-Lafi told US envoy Massad Boulos they 'reject any settlement based on limited understandings that could reproduce division.' High State Council member Nuh al-Malati said the council 'has not yet received an official copy' of the text and that the GNU-linked members who signed do not represent the HSC's official position. House of Representatives member Khalifa al-Daghari complained lawmakers learned details of the deal 'through the media' rather than a direct briefing. Legal expert Al-Mahdi Kashbour noted a gap between the signatories' authority and the institutions empowered to implement the deal, while analyst Elias al-Barouni said the pact contains no concrete election plan. UN spokesman Mohammad al-Asadi maintained it was 'an important step and a conclusion to the negotiations.'

title: Roadblocks and Burning Tyres Return to Tripoli Over Power Cuts
detail: Protesters blocked roads and burned tyres in several areas of Tripoli on August 25, reviving the civil disobedience campaign against prolonged electricity outages that began in late July. Demonstrators shut down major routes including the Nabras roundabout, roughly two kilometres from the Prime Minister's Office, and the Ghiran roundabout, one of the capital's main western entrances. No injuries or clashes with security forces were reported.
